newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Tranz Rail operating profit stays flat.
newsitem.headline: Tranz Rail operating profit stays flat.

text.p: Tranz Rail Holdings Ltd on Thursday reported a flat operating profit for the June year of NZ$73.2 million, while net profit rose to NZ$60.6 million from $49.18 million.
Chairman Edward Burkhardt said the operating result reflected the difficult low growth trading environment being experienced in New Zealand.
Revenue for the fourth quarter was $144.3 million, three percent greater than in the fourth quarter of 1996.
Total operating costs for the fourth quarter of the 1997 financial year increased 28 percent to $135.9 million from the $106.0 million reported for the same quarter of the previous year.
Tranz Rail, New Zealand's railways operator, is controlled by Wisconsin Central Transportation Corp.
Net profit for the last quarter was flat at NZ$15.9 million, or 16 cents per share.
Operating profit in the quarter fell 76 percent to $8.4 million, reflecting redundancy costs.
The quarterly result included several one-off events including a provision for redundancy costs of $13.2 million, and a $11.5 million recognition of deferred tax benefits.
Tranz Link revenue rose one percent in the quarter but there was downward pressure on freight rates.
Interisland passenger and vehicle revenue dipped for the quarter mainly due to seasonal holiday factors.
Total operating costs in the quarter rose 28 percent to $135.9 million due to higher labour costs, increased traffic and staff incentive plans.
